The application has grown and there are user complaints about internet bandwidth limitations. A solutions architect needs to design a long-term solution that allows for both timely backups to Amazon S3 and with minimal impact on internet connectivity for internal users. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: B. Establish a new AWS Direct Connect connection and direct backup traffic through this new connection.
options: Establish AWS VPN connections and proxy all traffic through a VPC gateway endpoint.
Establish a new AWS Direct Connect connection and direct backup traffic through this new connection.
Order daily AWS Snowball devices. Load the data onto the Snowball devices and return the devices to AWS each day.
Submit a support ticket through the AWS Management Console. Request the removal of S3 service limits from the account.
cards.explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated physical link between on-prem and AWS, bypassing the public Internet. Backup traffic flows over DX, freeing Internet bandwidth for users. Long-term solution. VPN (A) still uses the public Internet, doesn't free bandwidth. Daily Snowball (C) is operational nightmare for an ongoing backup workflow. Removing service limits (D) doesn't add bandwidth. Mental shortcut: 'large ongoing backup to AWS + don't saturate Internet' = AWS Direct Connect.
tricks: 'large ongoing backup to AWS + don't saturate Internet' = AWS Direct Connect

cards.q: A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains critical data. The company must protect the data from accidental deletion. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Enable versioning on the S3 bucket. ; B. Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket.
options: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket.
Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket.
Create a bucket policy on the S3 bucket.
Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket.
Create a lifecycle policy for the objects in the S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: Versioning (A) keeps every version including delete markers, so an accidental delete is just adding a marker that can be removed to restore. MFA Delete (B) requires the root account and an MFA token to permanently delete versions, making accidental destruction nearly impossible. Bucket policies (C) help with access control but don't recover deletions. Default encryption (D) protects confidentiality, not against deletion. Lifecycle (E) actually deletes objects on schedule, the opposite of protection. Mental shortcut: 'protect S3 from accidental deletion' = Versioning + MFA Delete.
tricks: 'protect S3 from accidental deletion' = Versioning + MFA Delete

cards.q: A company has a data ingestion workflow that consists of the following: • An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for notifications about new data deliveries • An AWS Lambda function to process the data and record metadata The company observes that the ingestion workflow fails occasionally because of network connectivity issues. When such a failure occurs, the Lambda function does not ingest the corresponding data unless the company manually reruns the job. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to ensure that the Lambda function ingests all data in the future? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue, and subscribe it to the SNS topic. ; E. Modify the Lambda function to read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.
options: Deploy the Lambda function in multiple Availability Zones.
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue, and subscribe it to the SNS topic.
Increase the CPU and memory that are allocated to the Lambda function.
Increase provisioned throughput for the Lambda function.
Modify the Lambda function to read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.
cards.explanation: Insert an SQS queue between SNS and Lambda: subscribe SQS to the SNS topic (B), and switch the Lambda event source to that SQS queue (E). SQS provides durable retries, DLQ, and decouples Lambda transient failures from message loss. Multi-AZ Lambda (A) is automatic and doesn't address message loss. CPU/memory (C) doesn't affect retry logic. Lambda has no 'provisioned throughput' setting (D). Mental shortcut: 'never lose a message + Lambda transient failures' = put SQS between SNS and Lambda.
tricks: 'never lose a message + Lambda transient failures' = put SQS between SNS and Lambda

cards.q: A company has an application that provides marketing services to stores. The services are based on previous purchases by store customers. The stores upload transaction data to the company through SFTP, and the data is processed and analyzed to generate new marketing offers. Some of the files can exceed 200 GB in size. Recently, the company discovered that some of the stores have uploaded files that contain personally identifiable information (PII) that should not have been included. The company wants administrators to be alerted if PII is shared again. The company also wants to automate remediation. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
cards.a: B. Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Macie to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.
options: Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Inspector to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the objects that contain PII.

Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Macie to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.

Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.

Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to trigger a notification to the administrators and trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the meats that contain PII.
cards.explanation: Amazon Macie automatically detects PII (and other sensitive data) in S3 buckets with managed ML, no custom code. Macie publishes findings to EventBridge which triggers SNS for admin alerts. Inspector (A) scans EC2/ECR for vulnerabilities, not S3 content. Custom Lambda PII scanners (C, D) require building and maintaining ML models. Mental shortcut: 'detect PII in S3 + LEAST development effort' = Macie + SNS.
tricks: 'detect PII in S3 + LEAST development effort' = Macie + SNS
'discover PII in S3' = Amazon Macie (NOT GuardDuty, NOT Inspector)

cards.q: A company needs guaranteed Amazon EC2 capacity in three specific Availability Zones in a specific AWS Region for an upcoming event that will last 1 week. What should the company do to guarantee the EC2 capacity?
cards.a: D. Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
options: Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region needed.
Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region needed.
Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
cards.explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservation guarantees EC2 capacity in specified AZs (you must specify AZ, not just Region) and can be created and released as needed. Reserved Instances (A, C) optimize cost over a 1-3 year term, not capacity guarantee for a 1-week event. RI in a Region without AZ (A) doesn't guarantee specific AZ capacity. ODCR at Region level (B) doesn't pin capacity to specific AZs. Mental shortcut: 'guaranteed EC2 capacity in specific AZs for a short event' = On-Demand Capacity Reservation with AZs.
tricks: 'guaranteed EC2 capacity in specific AZs for a short event' = On-Demand Capacity Reservation with AZs

cards.q: A company's website uses an Amazon EC2 instance store for its catalog of items. The company wants to make sure that the catalog is highly available and that the catalog is stored in a durable location. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. Move the catalog to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
options: Move the catalog to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
Deploy a larger EC2 instance with a larger instance store.
Move the catalog from the instance store to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Move the catalog to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
cards.explanation: Instance store is ephemeral (data lost on stop/terminate), not durable. EFS is a managed file system durable across multiple AZs, mountable from EC2 with NFS. Catalog stays accessible if any AZ fails. ElastiCache (A) is a cache, data isn't durable. Larger instance store (B) is still ephemeral. Glacier Deep Archive (C) has hour-scale retrieval, not viable for a website catalog. Mental shortcut: 'replace instance store + durable + highly available file access' = EFS.
tricks: 'replace instance store + durable + highly available file access' = EFS
'lowest latency + ephemeral OK' = EC2 Instance Store (lost on stop)

cards.q: A company stores call transcript files on a monthly basis. Users access the files randomly within 1 year of the call, but users access the files infrequently after 1 year. The company wants to optimize its solution by giving users the ability to query and retrieve files that are less than 1-year- old as quickly as possible. A delay in retrieving older files is acceptable. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: B. Store individual files in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files that are in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena. Query and retrieve the files that are in S3 Glacier by using S3 Glacier Select.
options: Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Query the tags to retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

Store individual files in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files that are in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena. Query and retrieve the files that are in S3 Glacier by using S3 Glacier Select.

Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Store search metadata for each archive in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files by searching for metadata from Amazon S3.

Store individual files in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Store search metadata in Amazon RDS. Query the files from Amazon RDS. Retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
cards.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering optimizes within the year-1 access window automatically. Lifecycle to Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year delivers cheap long-term storage. Athena queries the active S3 portion fast; Glacier Select queries the archived portion (delay acceptable). Glacier Instant Retrieval (A) gives ms access but costs more than Standard for files accessed randomly within a year. Standard + lifecycle to Instant Retrieval (C) doesn't optimize within year 1. Deep Archive + RDS metadata (D) adds DB ops overhead and 12+ hour retrieval is slower than Flexible. Mental shortcut: 'random access year 1 + cheap archive + queryable' = Intelligent-Tiering then Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
tricks: 'random access year 1 + cheap archive + queryable' = Intelligent-Tiering then Glacier Flexible Retrieval

cards.q: A company has a production workload that runs on 1,000 Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The workload is powered by third-party software. The company needs to patch the third-party software on all EC2 instances as quickly as possible to remediate a critical security vulnerability. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a custom command that applies the patch to all EC2 instances.
options: Create an AWS Lambda function to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
Schedule an AWS Systems Manager maintenance window to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a custom command that applies the patch to all EC2 instances.
cards.explanation: Critical security patch on 1000 instances ASAP = ad-hoc execution, not a scheduled flow. Systems Manager Run Command pushes commands or scripts to all targeted instances at once and is purpose-built for this. Patch Manager (B) is for OS patching with baselines, slower setup, and is for OS-level patches not third-party software. Maintenance windows (C) defer to a scheduled time, contradicting 'as quickly as possible'. Custom Lambda (A) reinvents Run Command. Mental shortcut: 'apply a patch to many EC2 NOW' = SSM Run Command.
tricks: 'apply a patch to many EC2 NOW' = SSM Run Command

cards.q: A company is developing an application that provides order shipping statistics for retrieval by a REST API. The company wants to extract the shipping statistics, organize the data into an easy-to-read HTML format, and send the report to several email addresses at the same time every morning. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email. ; D. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
options: Configure the application to send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email.
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Glue job to query the application's API for the data.
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
Store the application data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as an S3 event destination to send the report by email.
cards.explanation: EventBridge scheduled rule (D) invokes Lambda each morning. Lambda queries the API and gets the data. SES (B) formats the email and sends to multiple recipients (it natively supports HTML body and multiple To addresses). Kinesis Data Firehose (A) is streaming-to-storage, not for email reports. Glue (C) is ETL on data lakes, overkill. SNS as S3 destination (E) sends a notification, not a formatted HTML report by email. Mental shortcut: 'scheduled HTML email report' = EventBridge cron + Lambda + SES.
tricks: 'scheduled HTML email report' = EventBridge cron + Lambda + SES

cards.q: A company wants to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The application produces output files that vary in size from tens of gigabytes to hundreds of terabytes. The application data must be stored in a standard file system structure. The company wants a solution that scales automatically. is highly available, and requires minimum operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for storage.
options: Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon S3 for storage.
Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for storage.
Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
cards.explanation: Standard file system structure across multi-TB to PB with auto-scaling and HA = Amazon EFS, mountable from EC2 across AZs, scales to PB automatically. ECS + S3 (A) doesn't preserve standard POSIX file system structure. EKS + EBS (B) and EC2 + EBS (D) require manual EBS sizing per instance, not auto-scaling. Mental shortcut: 'POSIX file system + auto-scale to PB + HA' = EFS.
tricks: 'POSIX file system + auto-scale to PB + HA' = EFS
'minimum operational' = managed service (RDS over MySQL on EC2, Athena over EMR, etc.)

cards.q: A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional 9 years. No one at the company, including administrative users and root users, can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records must be stored with maximum resiliency. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
options: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.
cards.explanation: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode locks objects so even root cannot delete or overwrite during the retention period. Lifecycle to Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year handles the 9-year archive cheaply. Plain access policies (A) can be changed by root. IAM denies (B) can be removed by root. Governance mode (D) lets a privileged user with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention bypass it, breaking the 'no one, including root' requirement. Mental shortcut: 'no one can delete, including root, for N years' = Object Lock Compliance mode.
tricks: 'no one can delete, including root, for N years' = Object Lock Compliance mode
'block root user actions in member accounts' = SCP at Organizations level (only thing that constrains root)

cards.q: A company runs multiple Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use Windows file shares that are hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The file shares synchronize data between themselves and maintain duplicate copies. The company wants a highly available and durable storage solution that preserves how users currently access the files. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
options: Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.
cards.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server is a managed Windows-native SMB file system with built-in DFS, AD integration, and Multi-AZ deployment. Users keep accessing files via UNC paths exactly as before. EFS (D) is NFS/POSIX, not SMB-Windows-native. S3 + IAM (A) breaks SMB access pattern. S3 File Gateway (B) is for hybrid bridging, not the destination for cloud-native HA. Mental shortcut: 'managed Windows SMB shares + Multi-AZ' = FSx for Windows File Server.
tricks: 'managed Windows SMB shares + Multi-AZ' = FSx for Windows File Server

cards.q: A solutions architect is developing a VPC architecture that includes multiple subnets. The architecture will host applications that use Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The architecture consists of six subnets in two Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone includes a public subnet, a private subnet, and a dedicated subnet for databases. Only EC2 instances that run in the private subnets can have access to the RDS databases. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Create a security group that allows inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the private subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
options: Create a new route table that excludes the route to the public subnets' CIDR blocks. Associate the route table with the database subnets.
Create a security group that denies inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the public subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
Create a security group that allows inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the private subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
Create a new peering connection between the public subnets and the private subnets. Create a different peering connection between the private subnets and the database subnets.
cards.explanation: Security groups in AWS are stateful and reference other security groups. The right pattern: DB security group allows inbound on the DB port from the private-subnet EC2 security group. The DB SG implicitly denies everything else. Route table (A) doesn't enforce instance-level access control. Security groups don't have explicit deny rules (B). VPC peering (D) is between VPCs, not subnets in the same VPC. Mental shortcut: 'allow only specific instances to reach the DB' = DB SG references EC2 SG as source.
tricks: 'allow only specific instances to reach the DB' = DB SG references EC2 SG as source

cards.q: A company has registered its domain name with Amazon Route 53. The company uses Amazon API Gateway in the ca-central-1 Region as a public interface for its backend microservice APIs. Third-party services consume the APIs securely. The company wants to design its API Gateway URL with the company's domain name and corresponding certificate so that the third-party services can use HTTPS. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint.
options: Create stage variables in API Gateway with Name="Endpoint-URL" and Value="Company Domain Name" to overwrite the default URL. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point the alias record to the Regional API Gateway stage endpoint. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.

Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint.

Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway APIs. Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point an A record to the company's domain name.
cards.explanation: Regional API Gateway endpoint serves the same Region as ACM-imported certificate (regional certs must be in the same Region). Route 53 alias points the custom domain to the regional API Gateway endpoint. Stage variables (A) don't override the URL or handle TLS. ACM in us-east-1 (B, D) is required only for EDGE-optimized API Gateway endpoints (which use CloudFront). For regional endpoints the cert lives in the same Region. Mental shortcut: 'regional API Gateway + custom domain + HTTPS' = ACM cert in same Region + custom domain on API Gateway + Route 53 alias.
tricks: 'regional API Gateway + custom domain + HTTPS' = ACM cert in same Region + custom domain on API Gateway + Route 53 alias

cards.q: A company is running a popular social media website. The website gives users the ability to upload images to share with other users. The company wants to make sure that the images do not contain inappropriate content. The company needs a solution that minimizes development effort. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
options: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
Use Amazon SageMaker to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
Use AWS Fargate to deploy a custom machine learning model to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
cards.explanation: Amazon Rekognition Content Moderation API detects unsafe images (nudity, violence, etc.) out of the box with confidence scores. Below a threshold, route to Amazon Augmented AI for human review. Comprehend (A) is for text NLP, not images. SageMaker (C) requires training your own model. Custom Fargate model (D) is the most dev effort. Mental shortcut: 'inappropriate images + minimum dev effort' = Rekognition Content Moderation + A2I human review.
tricks: 'inappropriate images + minimum dev effort' = Rekognition Content Moderation + A2I human review

cards.q: A company wants to run its critical applications in containers to meet requirements for scalability and availability. The company prefers to focus on maintenance of the critical applications. The company does not want to be responsible for provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure that runs the containerized workload. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
options: Use Amazon EC2 instances, and install Docker on the instances.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
Use Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)-optimized Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
cards.explanation: Fargate is serverless containers: AWS provisions and manages the underlying infrastructure (no EC2 to patch, no nodes to scale). Pay per task-second. ECS on EC2 (B, D) requires managing EC2 worker nodes. EC2 + Docker (A) is fully self-managed. Mental shortcut: 'containers + don't manage infra' = Fargate (ECS or EKS).
tricks: 'containers + don't manage infra' = Fargate (ECS or EKS)

cards.q: A company hosts more than 300 global websites and applications. The company requires a platform to analyze more than 30 TB of clickstream data each day. What should a solutions architect do to transmit and process the clickstream data?
cards.a: D. Collect the data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to transmit the data to an Amazon S3 data lake. Load the data in Amazon Redshift for analysis.
options: Design an AWS Data Pipeline to archive the data to an Amazon S3 bucket and run an Amazon EMR cluster with the data to generate analytics.
Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to process the data and send it to an Amazon S3 data lake for Amazon Redshift to use for analysis.
Cache the data to Amazon CloudFront. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. When an object is added to the S3 bucket. run an AWS Lambda function to process the data for analysis.
Collect the data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to transmit the data to an Amazon S3 data lake. Load the data in Amazon Redshift for analysis.
cards.explanation: Standard streaming analytics pattern at 30 TB/day: Kinesis Data Streams ingests in real time, Firehose batches and lands data in S3, Redshift analyzes via COPY or Spectrum. Data Pipeline + EMR (A) is batch-oriented and partly deprecated. Auto Scaling EC2 (B) requires building the pipeline yourself. CloudFront caching for clickstream (C) is unrelated to ingestion. Mental shortcut: 'high-volume clickstream + analyze' = Kinesis Data Streams + Firehose + S3 + Redshift.
tricks: 'high-volume clickstream + analyze' = Kinesis Data Streams + Firehose + S3 + Redshift

cards.q: A company has a website hosted on AWS. The website is behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is configured to handle HTTP and HTTPS separately. The company wants to forward all requests to the website so that the requests will use HTTPS. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
cards.a: C. Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS.
options: Update the ALB's network ACL to accept only HTTPS traffic.
Create a rule that replaces the HTTP in the URL with HTTPS.
Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS.
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer configured to use Server Name Indication (SNI).
cards.explanation: ALB supports listener rules with a 'redirect' action that rewrites HTTP to HTTPS at the load balancer level, no app code change. Network ACL (A) blocks instead of redirecting. URL rewrite rules (B) on the app layer require code. NLB with SNI (D) doesn't redirect. Mental shortcut: 'redirect HTTP to HTTPS on ALB' = ALB listener rule with redirect action.
tricks: 'redirect HTTP to HTTPS on ALB' = ALB listener rule with redirect action

cards.q: A company is developing a two-tier web application on AWS. The company's developers have deployed the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that connects directly to a backend Amazon RDS database. The company must not hardcode database credentials in the application. The company must also implement a solution to automatically rotate the database credentials on a regular basis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: C. Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.
options: Store the database credentials in the instance metadata. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and instance metadata at the same time.

Store the database credentials in a configuration file in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and the credentials in the configuration file at the same time. Use S3 Versioning to ensure the ability to fall back to previous values.
Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.

Store the database credentials as encrypted parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation for the encrypted parameters. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the encrypted parameters.
cards.explanation: Secrets Manager natively supports automatic rotation for RDS via a managed Lambda rotation function and integrates with EC2 IAM roles for fetch-on-demand. No hardcoding, full rotation built-in. Parameter Store (D) does NOT auto-rotate arbitrary secrets, that's a Secrets Manager feature. Instance metadata (A) is for EC2 instance-identity data, not credentials. S3 + scheduled Lambda (B) reinvents Secrets Manager poorly. Mental shortcut: 'rotate DB credentials + LEAST overhead' = Secrets Manager.
tricks: 'rotate DB credentials + LEAST overhead' = Secrets Manager
'rotate credentials' or 'rotate password' = AWS Secrets Manager (native rotation)
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A company is deploying a new public web application to AWS. The application will run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application needs to be encrypted at the edge with an SSL/TLS certificate that is issued by an external certificate authority (CA). The certificate must be rotated each year before the certificate expires. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to import an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send a notification when the certificate is nearing expiration. Rotate the certificate manually.
options: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.

Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Import the key material from the certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALUse the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.

Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private Certificate Authority to issue an SSL/TLS certificate from the root CA. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.

Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to import an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send a notification when the certificate is nearing expiration. Rotate the certificate manually.
cards.explanation: ACM only manages auto-renewal for certificates ACM ISSUED itself (public CA, not external CA). When the cert is from an external CA you must IMPORT it, and ACM does not auto-renew imported certs. So the only viable rotation strategy is manual: import + EventBridge expiration alert. ACM-issued (A, B) ignores the requirement that cert is from external CA. Private CA (C) is internal-only certs, not external CA. Mental shortcut: 'cert from external CA + ACM' = import + manual rotation with expiration alert.
tricks: 'cert from external CA + ACM' = import + manual rotation with expiration alert

cards.q: A company runs its infrastructure on AWS and has a registered base of 700,000 users for its document management application. The company intends to create a product that converts large .pdf files to .jpg image files. The .pdf files average 5 MB in size. The company needs to store the original files and the converted files. A solutions architect must design a scalable solution to accommodate demand that will grow rapidly over time. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: A. Save the .pdf files to Amazon S3. Configure an S3 PUT event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in Amazon S3.
options: Save the .pdf files to Amazon S3. Configure an S3 PUT event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in Amazon S3.
Save the .pdf files to Amazon DynamoDUse the DynamoDB Streams feature to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in DynamoDB.

Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the files to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.

Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the file to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.
cards.explanation: S3 + Lambda is fully serverless, scales horizontally per file, pay only per invocation and storage. S3 PUT event triggers Lambda which converts and writes back to S3. DynamoDB (B) is for key-value data, storing 5MB blobs costs more and isn't the right tool. Beanstalk + EC2 + EBS (C, D) means running EC2 24/7 to wait for uploads, not cost-effective. Mental shortcut: 'on-demand file processing + scale + cheapest' = S3 + Lambda.
tricks: 'on-demand file processing + scale + cheapest' = S3 + Lambda

cards.q: A company has more than 5 TB of file data on Windows file servers that run on premises. Users and applications interact with the data each day. The company is moving its Windows workloads to AWS. As the company continues this process, the company requires access to AWS and on- premises file storage with minimum latency. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead and requires no significant changes to the existing file access patterns. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection for connectivity to AWS. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Deploy and configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the FSx File Gateway. Configure the cloud workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Configure the on- premises workloads to use the FSx File Gateway.
options: Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Move the on-premises file data to FSx for Windows File Server. Reconfigure the workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS.

Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the S3 File Gateway. Reconfigure the on- premises workloads and the cloud workloads to use the S3 File Gateway.

Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to Amazon S3. Reconfigure the workloads to use either Amazon S3 directly or the S3 File Gateway. depending on each workload's location.

Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Deploy and configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the FSx File Gateway. Configure the cloud workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Configure the on- premises workloads to use the FSx File Gateway.
cards.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server in AWS + FSx File Gateway on premises gives the lowest-latency hybrid Windows file access. The on-prem FSx File Gateway caches frequently used data locally so on-prem workloads have minimum latency, and the AWS FSx for Windows is the durable backend. S3 File Gateway (B, C) is SMB but not native Windows FSx, breaks Windows-specific features (DFS, NTFS ACLs). FSx without gateway (A) leaves on-prem accessing across the VPN with high latency. Mental shortcut: 'hybrid Windows file storage + low latency on both sides' = FSx for Windows + FSx File Gateway.
tricks: 'hybrid Windows file storage + low latency on both sides' = FSx for Windows + FSx File Gateway

cards.q: A hospital recently deployed a RESTful API with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The hospital uses API Gateway and Lambda to upload reports that are in PDF format and JPEG format. The hospital needs to modify the Lambda code to identify protected health information (PHI) in the reports. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: C. Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
options: Use existing Python libraries to extract the text from the reports and to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon SageMaker to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
Use Amazon Rekognition to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
cards.explanation: Textract extracts text from PDF and image documents. Comprehend Medical is the AWS managed service that detects PHI (protected health information) in medical text per HIPAA standards. Pure managed services, zero ML training. SageMaker (B) requires building and training a custom model. Custom Python libs (A) are dev effort. Rekognition (D) is for image objects/scenes, not generic OCR. Mental shortcut: 'extract text from documents + identify PHI' = Textract + Comprehend Medical.
tricks: 'extract text from documents + identify PHI' = Textract + Comprehend Medical
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A company has an application that generates a large number of files, each approximately 5 MB in size. The files are stored in Amazon S3. Company policy requires the files to be stored for 4 years before they can be deleted. Immediate accessibility is always required as the files contain critical business data that is not easy to reproduce. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of the object creation but are rarely accessed after the first 30 days. Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?
cards.a: C. Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
options: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.

Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier 4 years after object creation.
cards.explanation: Files frequently accessed first 30 days then rarely + must remain immediately accessible for 4 years total = Standard for 30 days, then Standard-IA. S3 Glacier (A, D) doesn't allow immediate access (retrieval times in minutes to hours). One Zone-IA (B) loses one AZ resilience for critical business data. Lifecycle ending in Glacier at year 4 (D) breaks immediate accessibility. Mental shortcut: 'always immediately accessible + cold after 30 days + multi-AZ resilience' = Standard then Standard-IA.
tricks: 'always immediately accessible + cold after 30 days + multi-AZ resilience' = Standard then Standard-IA

cards.q: A company hosts an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue, writes to an Amazon RDS table, and deletes the message from the queue. Occasional duplicate records are found in the RDS table. The SQS queue does not contain any duplicate messages. What should a solutions architect do to ensure messages are being processed once only?
cards.a: D. Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API call to increase the visibility timeout.
options: Use the CreateQueue API call to create a new queue.
Use the AddPermission API call to add appropriate permissions.
Use the ReceiveMessage API call to set an appropriate wait time.
Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API call to increase the visibility timeout.
cards.explanation: Duplicates in RDS but no duplicates in SQS = consumer is processing the same message twice. SQS standard delivers at-least-once: if a worker takes longer than the visibility timeout, the message becomes visible again and another worker picks it up. Increase visibility timeout to exceed actual processing time and the duplicate disappears. CreateQueue (A) and AddPermission (B) are unrelated. ReceiveMessage wait time (C) is long polling, controls poll latency, not duplicate processing. Mental shortcut: 'SQS duplicate processing without duplicate messages' = increase visibility timeout.
tricks: 'SQS duplicate processing without duplicate messages' = increase visibility timeout

cards.q: A solutions architect is designing a new hybrid architecture to extend a company's on-premises infrastructure to AWS. The company requires a highly available connection with consistent low latency to an AWS Region. The company needs to minimize costs and is willing to accept slower traffic if the primary connection fails. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: A. Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
options: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
Provision a VPN tunnel connection to a Region for private connectivity. Provision a second VPN tunnel for private connectivity and as a backup if the primary VPN connection fails.
Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a second Direct Connect connection to the same Region as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.

Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Use the Direct Connect failover attribute from the AWS CLI to automatically create a backup connection if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
cards.explanation: Direct Connect for low-latency primary, VPN as cheap backup is the canonical AWS hybrid HA pattern. Two Direct Connects (C) is most resilient but doesn't 'minimize cost' since DX is expensive. Two VPNs (B) lacks the consistent low latency the question requires. There is no 'failover attribute' in Direct Connect (D). Mental shortcut: 'low latency primary + cheap backup + accept slower failover traffic' = Direct Connect + VPN backup.
tricks: 'low latency primary + cheap backup + accept slower failover traffic' = Direct Connect + VPN backup

cards.q: A company is running a business-critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database that is deployed in a single Availability Zone. The company wants the application to be highly available with minimum downtime and minimum loss of data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
cards.a: B. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the database as Multi-AZ. Configure an Amazon RDS Proxy instance for the database.
options: Place the EC2 instances in different AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks to redirect traffic. Use Aurora PostgreSQL Cross- Region Replication.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the database as Multi-AZ. Configure an Amazon RDS Proxy instance for the database.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use one Availability Zone. Generate hourly snapshots of the database. Recover the database from the snapshots in the event of a failure.

Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple AWS Regions. Write the data from the application to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to launch an AWS Lambda function to write the data to the database.
cards.explanation: Multi-AZ Aurora + RDS Proxy + Multi-AZ ASG keeps the entire stack within a single Region, eliminates single-AZ failure as a downtime cause, and preserves connections during failover via RDS Proxy. Cross-Region (A, D) is heavier ops with Region failover orchestration, more than required. Single AZ + hourly snapshots (C) loses up to 1 hour of data and is not HA. Mental shortcut: 'minimum downtime + minimum data loss + LEAST effort' = Multi-AZ at the AZ level, not cross-Region.
tricks: 'minimum downtime + minimum data loss + LEAST effort' = Multi-AZ at the AZ level, not cross-Region

cards.q: A company's HTTP application is behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The NLB's target group is configured to use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with multiple EC2 instances that run the web service. The company notices that the NLB is not detecting HTTP errors for the application. These errors require a manual restart of the EC2 instances that run the web service. The company needs to improve the application's availability without writing custom scripts or code. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer. Enable HTTP health checks by supplying the URL of the company's application. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances.
options: Enable HTTP health checks on the NLB, supplying the URL of the company's application.
Add a cron job to the EC2 instances to check the local application's logs once each minute. If HTTP errors are detected. the application will restart.
Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer. Enable HTTP health checks by supplying the URL of the company's application. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances.
Create an Amazon Cloud Watch alarm that monitors the UnhealthyHostCount metric for the NLB. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances when the alarm is in the ALARM state.
cards.explanation: NLB does TCP/UDP health checks, not HTTP, so it can't detect application-layer errors. Replace with ALB which does HTTP health checks against a URL, and connect Auto Scaling to replace instances flagged unhealthy by the ALB. NLB HTTP health checks (A) don't exist. Cron + restart (B) requires custom code. UnhealthyHostCount alarm (D) doesn't trigger because NLB never sees the app errors. Mental shortcut: 'detect HTTP errors + auto-replace instances + no code' = ALB with HTTP health check.
tricks: 'detect HTTP errors + auto-replace instances + no code' = ALB with HTTP health check

cards.q: A company runs a shopping application that uses Amazon DynamoDB to store customer information. In case of data corruption, a solutions architect needs to design a solution that meets a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour. What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery. For RPO recovery, restore to the desired point in time.
options: Configure DynamoDB global tables. For RPO recovery, point the application to a different AWS Region.
Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery. For RPO recovery, restore to the desired point in time.
Export the DynamoDB data to Amazon S3 Glacier on a daily basis. For RPO recovery, import the data from S3 Glacier to DynamoDB.
Schedule Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots for the DynamoDB table every 15 minutes. For RPO recovery, restore the DynamoDB table by using the EBS snapshot.
cards.explanation: DynamoDB Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) provides continuous backups with restore to any second within the last 35 days, RPO of seconds, RTO of minutes-to-hours. Perfectly meets RPO 15 min and RTO 1 hour. Global tables (A) replicate across Regions but corruption replicates too, doesn't help with data corruption. Glacier daily exports (C) gives 24-hour RPO, fails the 15-min RPO. EBS snapshots are not for DynamoDB (D). Mental shortcut: 'data corruption recovery in DynamoDB + tight RPO' = DynamoDB Point-In-Time Recovery.
tricks: 'data corruption recovery in DynamoDB + tight RPO' = DynamoDB Point-In-Time Recovery

cards.q: A company runs a photo processing application that needs to frequently upload and download pictures from Amazon S3 buckets that are located in the same AWS Region. A solutions architect has noticed an increased cost in data transfer fees and needs to implement a solution to reduce these costs. How can the solutions architect meet this requirement?
cards.a: D. Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
options: Deploy Amazon API Gateway into a public subnet and adjust the route table to route S3 calls through it.
Deploy a NAT gateway into a public subnet and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
Deploy the application into a public subnet and allow it to route through an internet gateway to access the S3 buckets.
Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
cards.explanation: Within-Region S3 traffic from EC2 going through NAT or IGW incurs data processing fees. A Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 routes traffic privately and is FREE (no data processing fees). API Gateway (A) is unrelated. NAT gateway (B) charges processing. Internet gateway (C) traffic to S3 in same Region is technically free but goes over the public path; gateway endpoint is the canonical optimization. Mental shortcut: 'reduce data transfer cost to S3 from VPC' = Gateway VPC Endpoint.
tricks: 'reduce data transfer cost to S3 from VPC' = Gateway VPC Endpoint

cards.q: A company recently launched Linux-based application instances on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet and launched a Linux-based bastion host on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet of a VPC. A solutions architect needs to connect from the on-premises network, through the company's internet connection, to the bastion host, and to the application servers. The solutions architect must make sure that the security groups of all the EC2 instances will allow that access. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: C. Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company. ; D. Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
options: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the application instances.
Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the internal IP range for the company.
Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company.
Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the public IP address of the bastion host.
cards.explanation: Bastion is in a public subnet and is reached from on-premises over the internet, so its security group must allow inbound from the company's EXTERNAL (public) IP range (C), not the internal range (B). The application instances in the private subnet receive SSH from the bastion using its PRIVATE IP (D), because intra-VPC traffic uses private addressing. ExamTopics consensus: CD.
tricks: 'bastion = external company IP, app = bastion private IP'

cards.q: A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application consists of a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 in public subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet. Security is a high priority for the company. How should security groups be configured in this situation? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. ; C. Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
options: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
cards.explanation: Web tier security group: allow inbound 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 to expose HTTPS publicly (A). Database tier security group: allow inbound 1433 (SQL Server port) only from the web-tier security group (C). Outbound on web tier (B) is irrelevant for accepting traffic. Database outbound to web (D) is unnecessary because SGs are stateful (responses are auto-allowed). Database inbound on 443 (E) is wrong, DB doesn't serve HTTPS. Mental shortcut: 'web SG inbound 443 from anywhere, DB SG inbound DB port from web SG'.
tricks: 'web SG inbound 443 from anywhere, DB SG inbound DB port from web SG'

cards.q: A company wants to move a multi-tiered application from on premises to the AWS Cloud to improve the application's performance. The application consists of application tiers that communicate with each other by way of RESTful services. Transactions are dropped when one tier becomes overloaded. A solutions architect must design a solution that resolves these issues and modernizes the application. Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?
cards.a: A. Use Amazon API Gateway and direct transactions to the AWS Lambda functions as the application layer. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.
options: Use Amazon API Gateway and direct transactions to the AWS Lambda functions as the application layer. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.

Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze the application performance history to determine the servers' peak utilization during the performance failures. Increase the size of the application server's Amazon EC2 instances to meet the peak requirements.

Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SNS queue length and scale up and down as required.

Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SQS queue length and scale up when communication failures are detected.
cards.explanation: API Gateway + Lambda + SQS is the modern serverless decoupled architecture: API Gateway scales requests, Lambda runs the logic stateless, SQS buffers between tiers so a slow consumer never drops upstream traffic. SNS (C) is fan-out without buffering, transactions still drop. SQS + EC2 ASG (D) keeps EC2 management overhead. Resizing EC2 (B) is band-aid scaling, not modernization. Mental shortcut: 'modernize multi-tier + don't drop transactions + LEAST ops' = API Gateway + Lambda + SQS.
tricks: 'modernize multi-tier + don't drop transactions + LEAST ops' = API Gateway + Lambda + SQS

cards.q: A company receives 10 TB of instrumentation data each day from several machines located at a single factory. The data consists of JSON files stored on a storage area network (SAN) in an on-premises data center located within the factory. The company wants to send this data to Amazon S3 where it can be accessed by several additional systems that provide critical near-real-time analytics. A secure transfer is important because the data is considered sensitive. Which solution offers the MOST reliable data transfer?
cards.a: B. AWS DataSync over AWS Direct Connect
options: AWS DataSync over public internet
AWS DataSync over AWS Direct Connect
AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over public internet
AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over AWS Direct Connect
cards.explanation: 10 TB/day of sensitive data + reliability + secure = AWS DataSync (purpose-built file/object transfer with integrity verification) over Direct Connect (private, dedicated, high-bandwidth). DataSync over public Internet (A) is less reliable and saturates the public link. DMS (C, D) is for database migration, not file/JSON transfer. Mental shortcut: 'high-volume secure file transfer to S3' = DataSync over Direct Connect.
tricks: 'high-volume secure file transfer to S3' = DataSync over Direct Connect

cards.q: A company needs to configure a real-time data ingestion architecture for its application. The company needs an API, a process that transforms data as the data is streamed, and a storage solution for the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: C. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
options: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to AWS Glue. Stop source/destination checking on the EC2 instance. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to send the data to Amazon S3.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to AWS Glue. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use AWS Glue to send the data to Amazon S3.
cards.explanation: API Gateway as the API layer (managed, no servers), Kinesis Data Streams + Firehose for streaming with Lambda transformations, S3 for storage. Pure serverless. Option A puts API on EC2, adding management overhead. Glue (B, D) is ETL on data lakes, not a real-time streaming destination. Mental shortcut: 'real-time API + transform + store + LEAST ops' = API Gateway + Kinesis Data Streams + Firehose with Lambda + S3.
tricks: 'real-time API + transform + store + LEAST ops' = API Gateway + Kinesis Data Streams + Firehose with Lambda + S3
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A company needs to keep user transaction data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must retain the data for 7 years. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?
cards.a: B. Use AWS Backup to create backup schedules and retention policies for the table.
options: Use DynamoDB point-in-time recovery to back up the table continuously.
Use AWS Backup to create backup schedules and retention policies for the table.
Create an on-demand backup of the table by using the DynamoDB console. Store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to back up the table and to store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: AWS Backup natively supports DynamoDB, lets you set retention up to indefinite (handles 7 years easily), and centralizes backup schedules + retention policies across services. PITR (A) only retains 35 days, can't reach 7 years. On-demand backups + Lifecycle to S3 (C) and Lambda DIY (D) are operationally heavy. Mental shortcut: 'retain DynamoDB backups for years + LEAST ops' = AWS Backup.
tricks: 'retain DynamoDB backups for years + LEAST ops' = AWS Backup

cards.q: A company is planning to use an Amazon DynamoDB table for data storage. The company is concerned about cost optimization. The table will not be used on most mornings. In the evenings, the read and write traffic will often be unpredictable. When traffic spikes occur, they will happen very quickly. What should a solutions architect recommend?
cards.a: A. Create a DynamoDB table in on-demand capacity mode.
options: Create a DynamoDB table in on-demand capacity mode.
Create a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index.
Create a DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity and auto scaling.
Create a DynamoDB table in provisioned capacity mode, and configure it as a global table.
cards.explanation: On-demand capacity mode auto-scales to handle any traffic with zero capacity planning, perfect for unpredictable spiky workloads with idle periods (no minimum charge). Provisioned + auto-scaling (C) responds in minutes, too slow for 'spike very quickly' and you still pay baseline. Global tables (D) are for multi-Region, not capacity. GSI (B) is an indexing feature, not a capacity model. Mental shortcut: 'unpredictable spiky DynamoDB traffic with idle periods' = On-demand capacity.
tricks: 'unpredictable spiky DynamoDB traffic with idle periods' = On-demand capacity
'DynamoDB unpredictable load' = On-Demand mode (no capacity planning)
'DynamoDB predictable load' = Provisioned mode + auto scaling (cheaper than On-Demand)

cards.q: A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP) Partner for help with an application migration initiative. A solutions architect needs ta share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt EBS volume snapshots. What is the MOST secure way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account?
cards.a: B. Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
options: Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.

Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account.
cards.explanation: Most secure share: modify the AMI launchPermission to share specifically with the partner's AWS account (not public), then update the KMS key policy to grant the partner account permission to use the key. Partner can launch the AMI by decrypting snapshots. Public AMI (A) violates the security requirement. Trusting partner's KMS (C) doesn't work because snapshots are still encrypted with the source key. S3 export (D) is unnecessary complexity. Mental shortcut: 'share encrypted AMI securely with another account' = AMI launchPermission to that account + KMS key policy grants that account.
tricks: 'share encrypted AMI securely with another account' = AMI launchPermission to that account + KMS key policy grants that account
'customer managed key' or 'control rotation' = KMS customer managed key (CMK)

cards.q: A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new application being deployed on AWS. The process should run in parallel while adding and removing application nodes as needed based on the number of jobs to be processed. The processor application is stateless. The solutions architect must ensure that the application is loosely coupled and the job items are durably stored. Which design should the solutions architect use?
cards.a: C. Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of items in the SQS queue.
options: Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on CPU usage.

Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on network usage.

Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of items in the SQS queue.

Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.
cards.explanation: SQS for durable job queue + Auto Scaling group with launch template scaling on queue depth = canonical async worker pattern. Stateless workers scale horizontally with the backlog. SNS (A, D) is pub/sub, not durable job storage. Launch configurations (A, B) are deprecated, use launch templates. Scaling on CPU/network (A, B) is indirect, the queue length is the direct signal. Mental shortcut: 'parallel stateless workers + durable jobs + scale on backlog' = SQS + ASG with launch template + scale on queue depth.
tricks: 'parallel stateless workers + durable jobs + scale on backlog' = SQS + ASG with launch template + scale on queue depth
'loose coupling' = put a queue (SQS) or event bus (EventBridge/SNS) between producer and consumer

cards.q: A company hosts its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). The company's security team must be notified 30 days before the expiration of each certificate. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?
cards.a: B. Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.
options: Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.

Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.

Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
cards.explanation: AWS Config has a purpose-built managed rule 'acm-certificate-expiration-check' that flags ACM certificates expiring within a specified number of days. Pair it with EventBridge reacting to the noncompliant finding plus SNS for the alert. No custom code. D is wrong: EventBridge is an event router, it does not itself evaluate certificate expiry, and it forces a custom Lambda (more overhead). A (ACM publishing daily to SNS) is not a real ACM feature. Source: docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/acm-certificate-expiration-check.html
tricks: 'alert before ACM expiry' = EventBridge rule on ACM expiration event + Lambda/SNS

cards.q: A company's dynamic website is hosted using on-premises servers in the United States. The company is launching its product in Europe, and it wants to optimize site loading times for new European users. The site's backend must remain in the United States. The product is being launched in a few days, and an immediate solution is needed. What should the solutions architect recommend?
cards.a: C. Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.
options: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in us-east-1 and migrate the site to it.
Move the website to Amazon S3. Use Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.
Use an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy pointing to on-premises servers.
cards.explanation: CloudFront with custom origin pointing to on-prem servers caches content at edges in Europe and reduces page-load times for European users immediately, with no migration. Backend stays on prem. EC2 in us-east-1 (A) requires migration in days, doesn't help Europe latency directly. S3 (B) doesn't host dynamic apps. Geoproximity (D) routes by location but doesn't accelerate the path or cache. Mental shortcut: 'optimize global latency for users + immediate + backend stays on prem' = CloudFront with custom origin.
tricks: 'optimize global latency for users + immediate + backend stays on prem' = CloudFront with custom origin

cards.q: A company wants to reduce the cost of its existing three-tier web architecture. The web, application, and database servers are running on Amazon EC2 instances for the development, test, and production environments. The EC2 instances average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during non-peak hours. The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day. The development and test EC2 instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not in use. Which EC2 instance purchasing solution will meet the company's requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: B. Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
options: Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.
cards.explanation: Production runs 24/7 = Reserved Instances (steady, predictable, big discount over 1 or 3 years). Dev/test runs at least 8h/day with stop-when-not-in-use = On-Demand (no commitment, no charge when stopped). Spot for production (A, C) violates uninterruptible production. Spot blocks (C, D) are a deprecated feature; even if available they're not for steady production or stoppable dev. Mental shortcut: 'steady prod + stoppable dev/test' = Reserved for prod + On-Demand for dev/test.
tricks: 'steady prod + stoppable dev/test' = Reserved for prod + On-Demand for dev/test

cards.q: A company has a production web application in which users upload documents through a web interface or a mobile app. According to a new regulatory requirement. new documents cannot be modified or deleted after they are stored. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
cards.a: A. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.
options: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.
Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive the documents periodically.
Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an ACL to restrict all access to read-only.
Store the uploaded documents on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Access the data by mounting the volume in read- only mode.
cards.explanation: S3 Versioning + Object Lock (in compliance or governance mode) makes objects immutable for a retention period, blocking modify and delete. This is the WORM pattern AWS provides. Lifecycle archive (B) doesn't prevent deletion. Versioning + ACL (C) doesn't lock objects, ACLs can be changed. EFS read-only mount (D) is a client-side hint, not enforced at storage layer.
