RTO of 4 hours is achievable. Lambda + custom scripts (A) reinvents CloudFormation. Always-on EC2 in second Region (C) wastes resources. Single AZ (D) doesn't address Region DR. Mental shortcut: 'DR with RTO < 4h + fewest resources running' = AMI + CloudFormation in DR Region.
tricks: 'DR with RTO < 4h + fewest resources running' = AMI + CloudFormation in DR Region

cards.q: A company runs an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff are complaining that the application is very slow when the day begins, although it runs well by mid-morning. How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints and keep costs to a minimum?
cards.a: A. Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
options: Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
cards.explanation: Predictable morning surge from 2 to 20 = scheduled action sets desired capacity to 20 at office open. Step/target tracking (B, C) react after the load arrives, lag during the surge. Setting min and max to 20 (D) traps the ASG at 20 even after demand falls. Mental shortcut: 'predictable surge at fixed time' = scheduled action setting desired capacity.
tricks: 'predictable surge at fixed time' = scheduled action setting desired capacity

cards.q: A company has a multi-tier application deployed on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Amazon RDS for Oracle instance is the application’ s data layer that uses Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions. Traffic to the application has been steadily increasing. This is causing the EC2 instances to become overloaded and the RDS instance to run out of storage. The Auto Scaling group does not have any scaling metrics and defines the minimum healthy instance count only. The company predicts that traffic will continue to increase at a steady but unpredictable rate before leveling off. What should a solutions architect do to ensure the system can automatically scale for the increased traffic? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Configure storage Auto Scaling on the RDS for Oracle instance. ; D. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average CPU as the scaling metric.
options: Configure storage Auto Scaling on the RDS for Oracle instance.
Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora to use Auto Scaling storage.
Configure an alarm on the RDS for Oracle instance for low free storage space.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average CPU as the scaling metric.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average free memory as the scaling metric.
cards.explanation: RDS storage Auto Scaling (A) automatically grows storage when needed. ASG with average CPU as scaling metric (D) handles compute scaling. Migrating Oracle to Aurora (B) is not feasible: question says Oracle PL/SQL is required. Free storage alarm (C) only alerts, doesn't scale. Memory metric (E) isn't built-in for EC2 (requires CloudWatch agent) and CPU is more standard. Mental shortcut: 'auto-scale RDS Oracle storage + ASG compute' = RDS Storage Auto Scaling + CPU scaling on ASG.
tricks: 'auto-scale RDS Oracle storage + ASG compute' = RDS Storage Auto Scaling + CPU scaling on ASG

cards.q: A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive. Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?
cards.a: D. Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.
options: Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.
cards.explanation: S3 stores video content cheaply. Move only the file being processed to a temporary EBS volume on the worker, then delete it. EFS Standard (C) is more expensive than S3 for bulk storage. Storage Gateway (A, B) is for hybrid on-prem connectivity. Mental shortcut: 'cheapest video storage with EC2 processing' = S3 + temporary EBS for processing.
tricks: 'cheapest video storage with EC2 processing' = S3 + temporary EBS for processing

cards.q: A company wants to create an application to store employee data in a hierarchical structured relationship. The company needs a minimum-latency response to high-traffic queries for the employee data and must protect any sensitive data. The company also needs to receive monthly email messages if any financial information is present in the employee data. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: B. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month. ; E. Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.
options: Use Amazon Redshift to store the employee data in hierarchies. Unload the data to Amazon S3 every month.
Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month.
Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly events to AWS Lambda.
Use Amazon Athena to analyze the employee data in Amazon S3. Integrate Athena with Amazon QuickSight to publish analysis dashboards and share the dashboards with users.
Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.
cards.explanation: DynamoDB stores hierarchical data (parent-child via partition keys + sort keys) with single-digit-ms latency and high traffic capacity (B). Macie + EventBridge + SNS sends monthly notifications when financial data is detected (E). Redshift (A) is OLAP, wrong fit. Macie + Lambda (C) requires custom code where SNS subscription is simpler. Athena + QuickSight (D) is analytics, not the requested 'low-latency app'. Mental shortcut: 'hierarchical low-latency app data + sensitive data alerting' = DynamoDB + Macie + SNS.
tricks: 'hierarchical low-latency app data + sensitive data alerting' = DynamoDB + Macie + SNS

cards.q: A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: A. Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
options: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.

Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.
cards.explanation: AWS Backup plans support DynamoDB with monthly schedules, lifecycle to cold storage after 6 months, and 7-year retention all in one managed service. On-demand backups + S3 transitions (B) is multi-step custom. Custom scripts (C, D) reinvent AWS Backup poorly. Mental shortcut: 'monthly DynamoDB backups + 6mo warm + 7yr retention + LEAST ops' = AWS Backup plan.
tricks: 'monthly DynamoDB backups + 6mo warm + 7yr retention + LEAST ops' = AWS Backup plan

cards.q: A company is using Amazon CloudFront with its website. The company has enabled logging on the CloudFront distribution, and logs are saved in one of the company’s Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to perform advanced analyses on the logs and build visualizations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
options: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
cards.explanation: Athena queries CloudFront logs in S3 with SQL (no data movement). QuickSight visualizes Athena results natively. DynamoDB doesn't query S3 logs (C, D). Glue (A) is for ETL, not visualization. Mental shortcut: 'analyze S3 logs with SQL + visualize' = Athena + QuickSight.
tricks: 'analyze S3 logs with SQL + visualize' = Athena + QuickSight
'reduce latency for global users' = CloudFront edge caching

cards.q: A company runs a fleet of web servers using an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. After a routine compliance check, the company sets a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: A. Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
options: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.
cards.explanation: Multi-AZ provides synchronous replication to a standby in another AZ, RPO essentially zero (every committed transaction is on the standby). Auto scaling (B) is for compute. Read replicas (C) are async. DMS CDC (D) is async stream. Mental shortcut: 'RPO < 1 second for RDS' = Multi-AZ synchronous replication.
tricks: 'RPO < 1 second for RDS' = Multi-AZ synchronous replication

cards.q: A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across the public subnets directs web traffic to the EC2 instances. The company wants to implement new security measures to restrict inbound traffic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
options: Configure a route in a route table to direct traffic from the internet to the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.
Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.
Configure the security group for the ALB to allow any TCP traffic on any port.
cards.explanation: EC2 SG allows inbound only from ALB SG, denying everything else (security groups are stateful and can reference other SGs). Route table for Internet to private IPs (A) is wrong, internet traffic doesn't directly route to private subnets. Public EC2 (C) defeats the purpose. ALB SG allowing all TCP (D) opens the wrong tier. Mental shortcut: 'restrict EC2 to only ALB traffic' = EC2 SG references ALB SG.
tricks: 'restrict EC2 to only ALB traffic' = EC2 SG references ALB SG

cards.q: A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system. The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.
options: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.

Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.
cards.explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports BOTH NFS and SMB on the same volume (multi-protocol), eliminating the dual-file-system problem. The Linux app uses NFS, the Windows app uses SMB, same data. Lambda (A) doesn't run desktop or long-running simulation apps. Container migration (B) requires code/deploy changes. SQS (C) doesn't expose a file system. Mental shortcut: 'multi-protocol NFS + SMB on same data + no code change' = FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
tricks: 'multi-protocol NFS + SMB on same data + no code change' = FSx for NetApp ONTAP
'Windows SMB share + AD' = FSx for Windows File Server
'multi-protocol NFS+SMB' = FSx for NetApp ONTAP

cards.q: As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: B. Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
options: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
cards.explanation: Cost Explorer can group costs by tag (user/department) and produce downloadable reports interactively. Most efficient. Athena (A) requires CUR setup. Bill download (C) is unsegmented. Budgets (D) is alerting, not reporting. Mental shortcut: 'cost report by user/department' = Cost Explorer.
tricks: 'cost report by user/department' = Cost Explorer
'alert when cost exceeds threshold' = AWS Budgets

cards.q: A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: B. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
options: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client- side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
cards.explanation: API Gateway + Lambda + SES is fully serverless, scales to zero, charges essentially nothing for <100 visits/month. ECS (A) requires running containers. Lightsail (C) charges hourly for an instance. EC2 LAMP (D) charges hourly. Mental shortcut: 'tiny dynamic backend + cheapest' = API Gateway + Lambda + SES.
tricks: 'tiny dynamic backend + cheapest' = API Gateway + Lambda + SES

cards.q: A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
options: Add an Application Load Balancer.
Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website’s SSL certificate.
cards.explanation: CloudFront caches by default. After deployments, the old cached content stays until TTL expires (or you invalidate). Create a CloudFront invalidation (e.g., /*) post-deploy to immediately serve the new content. ALB (A) is unrelated. ElastiCache (B) is DB caching. ACM (D) is SSL. Mental shortcut: 'CloudFront site not showing updates' = invalidate the cache.
tricks: 'CloudFront site not showing updates' = invalidate the cache
'expose Lambda as HTTPS webhook' = Lambda Function URL (no API Gateway needed)
'reduce latency for global users' = CloudFront edge caching

cards.q: A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
options: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.

Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.
cards.explanation: RDS for SQL Server doesn't expose Data Quality Services and limits native backup format access. Hosting SQL Server on EC2 preserves all features. FSx for Windows File Server gives shared file storage natively to Windows EC2. RDS (C, D) loses required SQL Server features. EFS (C) and EBS (D) are wrong file-sharing primitives for Windows. Mental shortcut: 'full SQL Server features + Windows file sharing' = SQL on EC2 + FSx for Windows.
tricks: 'full SQL Server features + Windows file sharing' = SQL on EC2 + FSx for Windows

cards.q: A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
options: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.
cards.explanation: EFS provides POSIX-compliant shared file system mountable on multiple Linux EC2 with no app changes. S3 (A, B) requires SDK access (app change). EBS (D) is single-attach (multi-attach is io1/io2 only and limited). Mental shortcut: 'shared Linux file store + no app change' = EFS.
tricks: 'shared Linux file store + no app change' = EFS

cards.q: A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?
cards.a: B. Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
options: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.
cards.explanation: Lambda execution role with the minimum needed S3 permissions on the specific bucket = least-privilege secure pattern. Bucket policy (A) without an identity is risky and not used as the primary mechanism. Embedded keys (C) is anti-pattern. IAM role with access to ALL buckets (D) violates least privilege. Mental shortcut: 'Lambda secure read of S3' = IAM role with scoped IAM policy.
tricks: 'Lambda secure read of S3' = IAM role with scoped IAM policy

cards.q: A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment. Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
options: Dedicated Instances only
On-Demand Instances only
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances
cards.explanation: On-Demand baseline (no commitment) + Spot for surge (cheap, interruptible) maximizes savings without long-term commitment. Reserved (D) is a commitment. Dedicated (A) is most expensive. Pure On-Demand (B) misses Spot savings. Mental shortcut: 'cost-save without commitment' = On-Demand + Spot.
tricks: 'cost-save without commitment' = On-Demand + Spot

cards.q: A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content that is hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who has access. Some of the company’s users are using a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some of the company’s users are unable to change the hardcoded URLs that they are using for access. Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the LEAST impact to the users? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Signed cookies ; B. Signed URLs
options: Signed cookies
Signed URLs
AWS AppSync
JSON Web Token (JWT)
AWS Secrets Manager
cards.explanation: Users on an HTTP client with no cookie support must be served with Signed URLs (B); users who cannot change hardcoded URLs must be served with Signed Cookies (A), which authorize access without altering the URL. JWT (D) is not a CloudFront content-protection mechanism. ExamTopics consensus: AB.
tricks: 'restrict CloudFront access without cookies + with hardcoded URLs' = Signed URLs + JWT auth via Lambda@Edge
'reduce latency for global users' = CloudFront edge caching

cards.q: A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. The company needs the ability to use SQL to query the transformed data. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3. ; B. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
options: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
cards.explanation: Kinesis Streams + Kinesis Data Analytics + Firehose to S3 + Athena (A) is the canonical Kinesis-based real-time pipeline. MSK + Glue + Athena (B) is the Kafka-based equivalent with Glue ETL. DMS (C) is for DB migrations, not streaming. RDS query editor (D, E) cannot query S3. Mental shortcut: 'real-time stream + transform + query SQL on S3' = Kinesis Streams+KDA+Firehose+Athena OR MSK+Glue+Athena.
tricks: 'real-time stream + transform + query SQL on S3' = Kinesis Streams+KDA+Firehose+Athena OR MSK+Glue+Athena

cards.q: A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: D. Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
options: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on- premises systems with local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
cards.explanation: Maintaining local access to ALL data while backing it up to AWS requires a Storage Gateway STORED volume gateway (D), which keeps a full copy of the data on premises and asynchronously backs it up to AWS. A cached volume (C) keeps only frequently accessed data locally. ExamTopics consensus: D.
tricks: 'on-prem volume backup with local cache + ongoing AWS sync' = Storage Gateway cached volume gateway

cards.q: An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet. How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
options: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: Gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps traffic on the AWS network with no Internet hop. Private hosted zone (A) is DNS, not connectivity. NAT gateway (C) traverses Internet. Site-to-Site VPN (D) is for on-prem-to-AWS, S3 is in AWS already. Mental shortcut: 'EC2 to S3 + no Internet' = Gateway VPC endpoint.
tricks: 'EC2 to S3 + no Internet' = Gateway VPC endpoint

cards.q: An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: B. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
options: Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.
Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.
Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.
cards.explanation: S3 Object Lambda lets you transform data at retrieval time per-application: the PII-needing app gets full data, the others get redacted views, all from the same single S3 dataset. LEAST ops, no duplicated storage. DynamoDB proxy (A) requires custom code. Three buckets (C) and three DynamoDB tables (D) duplicate data and ops. Mental shortcut: 'serve different views from one S3 dataset + redact PII' = S3 Object Lambda.
tricks: 'serve different views from one S3 dataset + redact PII' = S3 Object Lambda
'discover PII in S3' = Amazon Macie (NOT GuardDuty, NOT Inspector)
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC. What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: VPC peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs. Existing VPC is 192.168.0.0/24, so the new VPC must not overlap. /32 (A, C) is one IP, far below VPC minimum of /28 (and AWS VPC range is /16 to /28). Same CIDR (B) overlaps. 10.0.1.0/24 (D) is non-overlapping and within valid VPC sizing. Mental shortcut: 'smallest valid VPC CIDR' = /28; 'peering' = non-overlapping CIDR. The smallest answer here that satisfies both is the /24 in option D.
tricks: 'smallest valid VPC CIDR' = /28; 'peering' = non-overlapping CIDR. The smallest answer here that satisfies both is the /24 in option D
'2 VPCs connected, no SG ref across Regions' = VPC peering same Region, Transit Gateway peering across Regions

cards.q: A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
options: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization matric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.
cards.explanation: Auto Scaling group with target tracking on average CPU at 50% scales between 2 and 6 instances based on actual load, optimizing cost (idle most of the time means scale to min) and ensuring capacity for surges. Manual Lambda termination (A) is custom code. ASG without scaling policy (C) doesn't actually scale. Manual ops via SNS (D) is operationally heavy. Mental shortcut: 'auto-scale on CPU + cost optimal' = ASG + target tracking on CPU.
tricks: 'auto-scale on CPU + cost optimal' = ASG + target tracking on CPU

cards.q: A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone. Which solution will make the application highly available?
cards.a: C. Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
options: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.

Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
cards.explanation: Subnets are AZ-bound (one subnet exists in exactly one AZ; subnets cannot 'span' AZs). So provision a subnet in each AZ, configure ASG across both, configure RDS Multi-AZ. Subnet spanning AZs (B, D) is impossible. Direct EC2 connections to two networks for DB (A) doesn't address DB HA. Mental shortcut: 'app HA across 2 AZs' = subnet per AZ + ASG across both + RDS Multi-AZ.
tricks: 'app HA across 2 AZs' = subnet per AZ + ASG across both + RDS Multi-AZ
'highly available RDS' = Multi-AZ deployment (instance) or Multi-AZ DB cluster (readable standbys)

cards.q: A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data. Which solution will meet the performance requirements?
cards.a: B. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
options: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
cards.explanation: FSx for Lustre persistent SSD delivers sub-ms latency and 100s of GB/s throughput at scale. Native S3 integration imports/exports raw data. HDD (C) is throughput-cheaper but doesn't meet sub-ms latency. ONTAP (A, D) is for general-purpose enterprise, not extreme HPC throughput. Mental shortcut: 'sub-ms + 6 GB/s + Linux + S3 backed' = FSx for Lustre persistent SSD.
tricks: 'sub-ms + 6 GB/s + Linux + S3 backed' = FSx for Lustre persistent SSD

cards.q: A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: C. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
options: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.
cards.explanation: 24x7 always-on workload that runs for years = Reserved Instances on both layers gives the steepest discount. RDS On-Demand (B) leaves money on the table for a 24/7 DB. Spot (A) is wrong for a production app that runs 24/7 (interruptible). On-Demand EC2 (D) is more expensive than RIs for steady workloads. Mental shortcut: 'always-on legacy app + most cost-effective' = Reserved Instances (EC2 + RDS/Aurora).
tricks: 'always-on legacy app + most cost-effective' = Reserved Instances (EC2 + RDS/Aurora)

cards.q: A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share. The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days. Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. AWS DataSync
options: AWS Snowcone
Amazon FSx File Gateway
AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family
cards.explanation: DataSync is the AWS-managed file transfer service that maximizes throughput AND lets you throttle bandwidth (KB/s, MB/s) so you don't crush a shared link. It supports SMB/NFS, transfers 30 TB easily over 1 Gbps within 5 days. Snowcone (A) caps at 8 TB usable, can't fit 30 TB. FSx File Gateway (B) is for steady-state hybrid file access, not bulk migration. Transfer Family (D) is SFTP/FTPS, not optimized for bulk file system migration. Mental shortcut: 'bulk file migration + bandwidth throttling + max performance' = AWS DataSync.
tricks: 'bulk file migration + bandwidth throttling + max performance' = AWS DataSync

cards.q: A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format. Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions to maximize the performance and scalability of the app while minimizing operational overhead. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching. ; C. Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
options: Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.
Use AWS DataSync to replicate the video files across AW'S Regions in other S3 buckets.
Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
Deploy an Auto Sealing group of Amazon EC2 instances in Local Zones for content delivery and caching.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
cards.explanation: CloudFront caches video clips at edge locations close to mobile users, eliminating buffering from S3-direct retrieval (A). Elastic Transcoder converts raw video to mobile-optimized formats (HLS, smaller bitrates) so mobile devices play smoothly (C). DataSync to other Regions (B) is bulk migration, not user-facing delivery. EC2 in Local Zones (D) is for ultra-low-latency compute; CloudFront is the right edge solution for video. Auto Scaling EC2 for transcoding (E) is high overhead vs managed Elastic Transcoder. Mental shortcut: 'mobile video buffering' = CloudFront for delivery + Elastic Transcoder for format.
tricks: 'mobile video buffering' = CloudFront for delivery + Elastic Transcoder for format

cards.q: A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases. What should a solutions architect recommend?
cards.a: D. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
options: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.
Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
cards.explanation: ECS Fargate scales via Application Auto Scaling using target tracking policies (e.g., target 70% CPU): the service automatically adds/removes tasks to maintain the target metric, scales up AND down. Step scaling (C) is older and less efficient than target tracking. EC2 Auto Scaling (A, C) doesn't apply to Fargate (Fargate has no EC2 to scale). Lambda + CloudWatch (B) is a manual reinvention of what App Auto Scaling does natively. Mental shortcut: 'auto-scale ECS Fargate up and down on metrics' = Application Auto Scaling with target tracking.
tricks: 'auto-scale ECS Fargate up and down on metrics' = Application Auto Scaling with target tracking
'containers without managing servers' = ECS/EKS on AWS Fargate

cards.q: A company recently created a disaster recovery site in a different AWS Region. The company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a periodic basis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: A. Use AWS DataSync.
options: Use AWS DataSync.
Use AWS Snowball devices.
Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
cards.explanation: DataSync supports periodic NFS-to-NFS replication across Regions out of the box, fully managed, with bandwidth controls and incremental sync. Snowball (B) is offline, not periodic. Custom SFTP on EC2 (C) is high overhead. DMS (D) is for databases, not file systems. Mental shortcut: 'periodic NFS-to-NFS across Regions + LEAST overhead' = AWS DataSync.
tricks: 'periodic NFS-to-NFS across Regions + LEAST overhead' = AWS DataSync
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed. Which AWS solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: C. Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
options: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.
cards.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server is the fully managed AWS service that exposes SMB shares with native Windows ACLs and AD integration. Self-managed EC2 Windows shares (B) require OS patching and HA setup. DataSync (A) is a transfer task, not a file system. S3 mounted (D) doesn't speak SMB. Mental shortcut: 'SMB + fully managed' = Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
tricks: 'SMB + fully managed' = Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

cards.q: A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost- effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: A. Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
options: Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.
cards.explanation: A cluster placement group packs EC2 instances close together on the same network spine for the highest network throughput and lowest inter-instance latency, all within ONE AZ. Cross-AZ (B, C, D) introduces inter-AZ data transfer charges and adds latency, both contradicting the requirements. Partition placement groups (B) are for distributed systems wanting fault isolation, not max throughput. Mental shortcut: 'high network throughput + minimize inter-AZ data transfer costs' = single-AZ + cluster placement group.
tricks: 'high network throughput + minimize inter-AZ data transfer costs' = single-AZ + cluster placement group

cards.q: A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally. Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes
options: Amazon S3 File Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes
cards.explanation: Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in CACHED mode keeps the primary dataset in S3 and only the recently accessed data is cached locally, exactly the requirement. Stored volumes (C) keep the entire dataset locally and back up async to S3, opposite of what's wanted. S3 File Gateway (A) is for NFS/SMB, not iSCSI. Tape Gateway (B) is for backup/archive workflows. Mental shortcut: 'iSCSI + only recently accessed data stays local' = Volume Gateway cached volumes.
tricks: 'iSCSI + only recently accessed data stays local' = Volume Gateway cached volumes

cards.q: A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company’s finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts. The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs. Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running. ; C. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
options: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.
cards.explanation: Trusted Advisor checks for individual member accounts must be reviewed in the account where the resources actually run (A), not in the consolidated billing account. The relevant cost optimization check for unused/idle paid RDS capacity is 'Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization' (C), which suggests buying RIs to reduce cost on long-running RDS instances. Idle DB Instances (D) is also a valid Trusted Advisor check but the RI Optimization check is the canonical 'reduce RDS cost' answer. Redshift check (E) is unrelated. Mental shortcut: 'reduce RDS cost via Trusted Advisor' = run from the account that owns the RDS + RI Optimization check.
tricks: 'reduce RDS cost via Trusted Advisor' = run from the account that owns the RDS + RI Optimization check

cards.q: A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs. The solutions architect must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed. Which solution will accomplish this goal with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: A. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
options: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.
Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.
Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
cards.explanation: S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide visibility into S3 usage and activity (number of objects, size, access patterns), with advanced metrics that show buckets that are no longer accessed or rarely accessed. Zero infrastructure to manage. Other options like custom Athena queries on access logs require building dashboards. Mental shortcut: 'S3 access patterns insight + LEAST overhead' = S3 Storage Lens.
tricks: 'S3 access patterns insight + LEAST overhead' = S3 Storage Lens
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A company sells datasets to customers who do research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company hosts a web application that the customers use to purchase access to a given dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is made, customers receive an S3 signed URL that allows access to the files. The customers are distributed across North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce the cost that is associated with data transfers and wants to maintain or improve performance. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: B. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.
options: Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.

Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.

Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.
cards.explanation: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) is the AWS-managed solution that replicates objects automatically across Regions for DR, with versioning. Set it up once, no code, no schedule. Custom Lambda copy (A) is high overhead. Snowball (C) is for offline migration. AWS Backup with S3 cross-Region copy (D) is overhead vs native CRR. Mental shortcut: 'replicate S3 across Regions for DR + LEAST overhead' = S3 CRR.
tricks: 'replicate S3 across Regions for DR + LEAST overhead' = S3 CRR

cards.q: A company is using AWS to design a web application that will process insurance quotes. Users will request quotes from the application. Quotes must be separated by quote type, must be responded to within 24 hours, and must not get lost. The solution must maximize operational efficiency and must minimize maintenance. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: C. Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.
options: Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.

Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.

Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.
cards.explanation: Quotes must be separated by type, must NOT be lost, with least maintenance. A single SNS topic with SQS queues subscribed + SNS message filtering routes each quote type to its own durable SQS queue. SQS guarantees no message loss. B (Lambda + an SNS topic per quote type, no SQS) can lose messages if processing fails and proliferates topics. This is the exact scenario in the official AWS tutorial 'Filter Messages Published to Topics with SNS and SQS', which recommends single-topic + filtering over per-type topics. ExamTopics consensus (incl. identical SAA-C02 Q172) is C with 54+ votes.
tricks: 'WORM + cannot be deleted by ANYONE including root' = S3 Object Lock compliance mode

cards.q: A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances. Each EC2 instance has multiple Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) data volumes attached to it. The application’s EC2 instance configuration and data need to be backed up nightly. The application also needs to be recoverable in a different AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
cards.a: B. Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.
options: Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application’s EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Region.
Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.
Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.
Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application's EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Availability Zone.
cards.explanation: Backing up both the EC2 instance configuration and its EBS data nightly with cross-Region copy, most operationally efficiently, is AWS Backup with the EC2 instances added as resources (B). Adding only the EBS volumes (C) misses the instance configuration, and custom Lambda snapshot scripts (A) add overhead. ExamTopics consensus: B.
tricks: 'cross-Region DB DR + sub-second lag + fast failover' = Aurora Global Database

cards.q: A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company’s content on their mobile devices. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
options: Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
cards.explanation: Reaching millions of mobile users for authorized content streaming is served by Amazon CloudFront with signed URLs (C): the CDN scales globally and signed URLs restrict access to authorized users. A VPN (B/D) does not scale to millions of consumer devices. ExamTopics consensus: C.
tricks: 'track configuration changes over time + detect drift' = AWS Config

cards.q: A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns. The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future. Which service should a solutions architect recommend?
cards.a: B. Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
options: Amazon Aurora MySQL
Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
Amazon Redshift Spectrum
Amazon RDS for MySQL
cards.explanation: Migrating MySQL without choosing an instance type, with infrequent access and room to grow, points to Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL (B), which auto-scales capacity. Redshift Spectrum (C) is a data-warehouse query layer, not a MySQL target. ExamTopics consensus: B.
tricks: 'private VPC-to-AWS-service connectivity' = AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint)

cards.q: A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: D. Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
options: Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
cards.explanation: Amazon Inspector is the AWS vulnerability scanning service for EC2 and ECR, automated and continuous. Pair it with Lambda for automated report distribution. GuardDuty (C) is threat detection (network/account anomalies), not vulnerability scanning. Macie (B) is for sensitive data discovery in S3. Shield (A) is DDoS protection. Mental shortcut: 'scan EC2 for software vulnerabilities' = Amazon Inspector.
tricks: 'scan EC2 for software vulnerabilities' = Amazon Inspector

cards.q: A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
options: Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.
cards.explanation: Lambda triggered by SQS scales automatically with the queue depth, eliminates EC2 management, and pays only per invocation. Bigger EC2 (A) doesn't reduce ops cost. EventBridge to stop EC2 (B) introduces latency and complexity. SSM Run Command (D) is for ad-hoc commands, not continuous queue processing. Mental shortcut: 'process SQS messages + reduce ops cost + scale with growth' = Lambda with SQS event source.
tricks: 'process SQS messages + reduce ops cost + scale with growth' = Lambda with SQS event source

cards.q: A company uses a legacy application to produce data in CSV format. The legacy application stores the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can perform complex SQL queries to analyze data that is stored in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3 only. However, the COTS application cannot process the .csv files that the legacy application produces. The company cannot update the legacy application to produce data in another format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data that the legacy application produces. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: A. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
options: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.

Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.
cards.explanation: AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL service that can read CSV from S3, transform to Redshift-compatible format, and load to Redshift on a schedule. Zero infrastructure. Custom Python on EC2 (B) requires self-managing the cron and EC2. Lambda + DynamoDB (C) changes the data destination (the COTS app needs Redshift, not DynamoDB). EMR weekly (D) is heavy and slow. Mental shortcut: 'ETL CSV from S3 to Redshift on a schedule + LEAST overhead' = AWS Glue.
tricks: 'ETL CSV from S3 to Redshift on a schedule + LEAST overhead' = AWS Glue
'LEAST operational overhead' = pick the most managed/serverless option (Lambda > Fargate > ECS-EC2 > EC2)

cards.q: A company recently migrated its entire IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company discovers that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and modifying security group rules without using the appropriate change control process. A solutions architect must devise a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes. Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.a: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing. ; D. Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
options: Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.
Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.
Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail logs every API call (who did what, when), critical for auditing changes. AWS Config tracks the resulting resource configuration over time and supports rules for compliance. Together they give a complete inventory + change audit story. Trusted Advisor (C) is best-practice checks, not change tracking. EC2 data lifecycle (B) is for snapshots. CloudFormation (E) is IaC, not auditing. Mental shortcut: 'audit changes + track inventory and config' = CloudTrail + AWS Config.
tricks: 'audit changes + track inventory and config' = CloudTrail + AWS Config
'track config changes over time' = AWS Config; 'track API calls' = CloudTrail

cards.q: A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company’s security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?
cards.a: A. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
options: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.
cards.explanation: Systems Manager Session Manager opens a browser-based or CLI shell to EC2 instances using IAM permissions and the SSM agent, no SSH keys, no bastion, no inbound port 22. STS for one-time SSH (B) requires custom code. Bastions (C) still use shared SSH keys, doesn't solve the problem. Cognito + Lambda for SSH (D) is custom and complex. Mental shortcut: 'replace SSH key access + LEAST admin overhead' = SSM Session Manager.
tricks: 'replace SSH key access + LEAST admin overhead' = SSM Session Manager

cards.q: A company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-flight is lost. The company’s data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time. Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?
cards.a: A. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
options: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.
cards.explanation: Near-real-time querying with minimal data loss requires durable streaming, so publish to Kinesis Data Streams and query with Kinesis Data Analytics (A). Storing in an EC2 instance store (C) loses data on reboot and Firehose to S3 adds buffering latency. ExamTopics consensus: A.
tricks: 'near-real-time ingest + scalable query + minimal data loss' = Firehose to S3 + Athena

cards.q: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?
cards.a: D. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.
options: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.
cards.explanation: The bucket policy must deny PutObject when the request lacks the x-amz-server-side-encryption header, forcing every upload to specify encryption. The x-amz-acl header (A, B) controls ACLs, not encryption. aws:SecureTransport (C) enforces HTTPS in transit, not at-rest encryption. Mental shortcut: 'enforce encryption on every PUT' = deny when x-amz-server-side-encryption header is absent.
tricks: 'enforce encryption on every PUT' = deny when x-amz-server-side-encryption header is absent

cards.q: A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully. The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
cards.a: C. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.
options: Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.

Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.
cards.explanation: SQS decouples the upload acceptance (fast, returns success immediately) from the slow thumbnail generation (consumed asynchronously). Custom Lambda chained to upload (A) is technically possible but the user must wait for Lambda completion before getting a confirmation, breaking the requirement. Step Functions (B) orchestrates synchronously and is overkill for a single async dispatch. SNS (D) doesn't buffer; if the consumer is offline the message is lost. Mental shortcut: 'decouple slow processing from fast user response' = SQS queue.
tricks: 'decouple slow processing from fast user response' = SQS queue

cards.q: A company’s facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When badges are scanned, the readers send a message over HTTPS to indicate who attempted to access that particular entrance.
